## Analysis Summary

**Test image key features:**
- Field-level landscape view of a mid-to-late season soybean field
- Pronounced lower canopy yellowing/defoliation visible in foreground
- Upper canopy remains relatively green
- Diffuse pattern across the field (not distinct patches or row-specific patterns)
- Some scattered yellow-tan leaves throughout

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Strong match — the upper-right panel of the Septoria reference shows nearly identical field-level pattern with lower canopy yellowing while upper canopy stays green. The disease characteristically starts in the lower canopy and progresses upward under favorable conditions.
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Ruled out — SDS causes distinct interveinal chlorosis/necrosis (green veins with yellow/brown tissue between), not the general lower-canopy yellowing seen here.
- **Soybean_rust**: Ruled out — rust field views show more uniformly tan/brown advanced defoliation across the whole canopy.
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Ruled out — shows distinct dying rows, not diffuse lower canopy yellowing.
- **Soybean_Cyst_Nematode**: Ruled out — SCN shows distinct circular/lens-shaped patches, not the diffuse pattern here.
- **White_Mold, Phytophthora, Anthracnose**: All ruled out based on reference image comparison.

The field-level pattern of progressive lower-canopy yellowing/defoliation with upper canopy remaining green is the hallmark presentation of Septoria brown spot.
